skills.name: What re.ghidra.analyze really is
skills.description: Understand the tool before using it.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. re.ghidra.analyze is a Ghidra-STYLE headless analysis approximation: Ghidra itself is a desktop Java app and cannot run on-device.
2. The tool pipelines three stages: rabin2 -I (file identification, the language-detection analog), rabin2 -E -s (entrypoints and symbols), and r2 aaa/aa with afl (functions), axff~? (xref counts), izz~? (strings).
3. The bundled ghidra pack (analyzeHeadless, GHIDRA_HOME) exists for real headless runs via process.exec when JDK is provisioned.
4. Choose the right layer per task: metadata (rabin2), code analysis (r2), or true Ghidra decompilation (analyzeHeadless via JDK).
5. Never claim real Ghidra decompilation when only the r2 approximation ran; label the engine in every report.

skills.name: Ghidra pack readiness
skills.description: Verify the runtime pack before relying on real headless runs.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. runtime.info to check the ghidra pack (version 12.1.2, entrypoints analyzeHeadless + ghidraRun).
2. Verify java availability: the bundled JDK pack is required by analyzeHeadless.
3. If the pack is missing, trigger provisioning from Runtime UI (heavy pack; extracts after core packs).
4. Path layout: ghidra/support/analyzeHeadless; the tool env sets GHIDRA_HOME and puts ghidra/support on PATH.
5. Check provisioning status in logs before long analysis sessions.

skills.name: Analysis engine map
skills.description: Map each RE task to the right engine.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. File/section/symbol metadata: re.rabin2 (fast, no analysis pass needed).
2. Function discovery and xrefs: re.r2.analyze or re.ghidra.analyze stage 3 (r2 aaa).
3. Decompilation-grade output: real Ghidra headless via process.exec + JDK (when provisioned), or IDA idat64 if installed.
4. Managed (Java/Kotlin) views: jadx + javap proxies, not native disassembly.
5. IL2CPP managed views: re.il2cpp.metadata, not Ghidra.

skills.name: Ghidra-style quick start
skills.description: Run the standard first-pass analysis.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. re.ghidra.analyze with file_path; keep deep=true (default) for the aaa auto-analysis pass.
2. Read the three report sections in order: File Identification, Entrypoints & Symbols, Function Analysis (aaa).
3. Note the function count and xref counts (axff~?) as binary complexity indicators.
4. Pull the izz~? string listing for immediate recon leads.
5. Capture the report into a workspace file (file.write) for the evidence chain.

skills.name: Deep vs quick analysis
skills.description: Choose the right analysis level.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. deep=true runs r2 aaa (full auto-analysis: functions, refs, flags). Use for real analysis work.
2. deep=false runs r2 aa (basic) — use for quick metadata-only passes on huge binaries where aaa would take minutes.
3. Strategy: aa first to sanity-check the file loads, then aaa for the real pass.
4. For very large binaries, prefer targeted re.r2.analyze commands over full aaa.
5. Record which level ran; xref/function counts differ between aa and aaa.

skills.name: Output size management
skills.description: Handle the 120k default cap correctly.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. max_output clamps 10000..400000 chars; the report is truncated with a visible [report truncated at N chars] marker.
2. For big binaries, raise max_output toward 400000 rather than losing the function list.
3. Better: run stage-equivalents separately via re.rabin2 (metadata) and re.r2.analyze (targeted commands) to keep each output small.
4. Save truncated reports and re-run missing sections deliberately.
5. Never summarize from a truncated report without noting the truncation.

skills.name: Report anatomy
skills.description: Parse the three-stage report correctly.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Stage 1 (rabin2 -I): format, arch, bits, endian, OS, compiler, pic/relro/canary hardening flags.
2. Stage 2 (rabin2 -E -s): entrypoints plus symbol table — the naming layer for everything later.
3. Stage 3 (r2): afl function list, axff~? xref counts, izz~? strings.
4. Hardening flags from stage 1 (canary/PIC/RELRO/NX) shape exploitation-style assessments.
5. Use stage-2 addresses as inputs to re.ida.offset / re.mem.ida_correlate for runtime work.

skills.name: Real headless Ghidra runs
skills.description: Use analyzeHeadless via process.exec.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Confirm ghidra pack + JDK: runtime.info, then check ghidra/support/analyzeHeadless exists (runtime exposes it on PATH and sets GHIDRA_HOME).
2. Import and analyze: process.exec analyzeHeadless <project_dir> <project_name> -import <binary> -analysisTimeoutPerFile 600.
3. List functions after analysis: -postScript with a listing script, or re-import to the same project to reuse analysis.
4. Headless is slow on-device; prefer it only when r2 output is insufficient (e.g. decompiler-grade pseudocode needs).
5. Save project logs to the workspace; headless runs create project files — keep them in a dedicated directory.

skills.name: Headless post-scripts
skills.description: Extract structured results from headless runs.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. analyzeHeadless supports -postScript <script.py> (Jython) or .java scripts for custom extraction.
2. Common extracts: function lists with sizes, decompiled C for selected functions, defined strings, data type managers.
3. Write scripts to the workspace (file.write) and pass absolute paths.
4. Keep scripts side-effect free: read Program API, print results, no database mutations unless intended.
5. Capture script stdout into workspace files for the evidence chain.

skills.name: Headless decompilation
skills.description: Get decompiler-grade pseudocode.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Ghidra's decompiler is the main reason to run real headless Ghidra instead of the r2 approximation.
2. Use a post-script that iterates functions and calls DecompInterface to dump C-like pseudocode per function.
3. Target only the functions of interest (by name filter or address range) — full-binary decompilation is impractical on-device.
4. Pair with re.ghidra.analyze stage 2 symbol names to pick decompile targets.
5. Label output as Ghidra-decompiler-grade (distinct from r2 pdf-style disassembly).

skills.name: Project reuse strategy
skills.description: Reuse analysis databases across sessions.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Headless projects persist analysis; re-importing the same binary into the same project skips re-analysis.
2. Keep one project per binary version: <binary>.<version> naming in a dedicated workspace folder.
3. Verify reuse worked: second run should be much faster (no analysis phase).
4. Delete stale projects (file.delete) when the binary version is retired to save disk.
5. Record project paths in session notes.

skills.name: Ghidra vs IDA vs r2 vs built-in
skills.description: Choose engines deliberately per task.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Built-in ELF analyzer (re.ida.analyze): structure metadata, always available, no dependencies.
2. r2 (re.r2.analyze / re.ghidra.analyze): fast function discovery, xrefs, strings; no decompiler.
3. Ghidra headless: decompiler-grade pseudocode; heavy (JDK + pack); slow on-device.
4. IDA (idat64): alternative decompiler/xref engine when installed (check re.ida.capabilities).
5. State the engine per finding; never mix results without labeling.

skills.name: Native library workflow
skills.description: Analyze a .so end to end.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. re.rabin2 -I for hardening flags (canary/RELRO/NX) and architecture.
2. re.ghidra.analyze deep=true for the function inventory and strings.
3. Pick targets: exported JNI functions (Java_ prefixed) and interesting strings.
4. Deep dive: re.r2.analyze with targeted commands (pdf @ sym.func) or headless decompile for the chosen functions.
5. Runtime correlation when needed: re.ida.offset / re.mem.ida_correlate against a live process.

skills.name: JNI bridge mapping
skills.description: Map Java-to-native surfaces with the Ghidra-style flow.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Get native method declarations from the decoded smali (file.search '.method public native').
2. Stage-2 symbols from re.ghidra.analyze contain Java_<class>_<method> exports.
3. Pair declarations to exports; note RegisterNatives-based bindings that bypass static naming.
4. Mark unpaired natives as dynamic-registration candidates for runtime analysis.
5. Record the JNI map (java method -> native symbol -> address).

skills.name: String-driven analysis
skills.description: Turn izz~? output into analysis leads.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Stage-3 izz~? strings reveal endpoints, file paths, version strings, and error messages.
2. Cross-reference interesting strings: re.r2.analyze with 'izz' then 'axt @ <addr>' for code references.
3. Classify: config markers, crypto hints (AES/RC4 constants), anti-debug messages.
4. Feed crypto-looking constants into the wider analysis (cat_re2_crypto_detect).
5. Record leads with their string addresses for the report.

skills.name: Hardening assessment
skills.description: Read the hardening story from stage 1.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. rabin2 -I exposes: canary (stack protector), nx, pic/PIE, relro (partial/full), and stripped status.
2. Map each flag to its meaning: canary=stack-overflow mitigation, full RELRO=GOT protection, PIC=ASLR-compatible.
3. Missing mitigations are findings for defensive reports; their presence shapes exploitation work.
4. Correlate with build config when the binary is your own (file.read build flags).
5. Record the hardening table per binary.

skills.name: Ghidra + IL2CPP pairing
skills.description: Analyze Unity games with the right split.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Managed view: re.il2cpp.metadata gives classes/methods/fields from global-metadata.dat — never re-derive these in Ghidra.
2. Native view: re.ghidra.analyze stage 2-3 for libil2cpp.so symbols (il2cpp_*, CodeGen*) and function inventory.
3. Bridge: method native_symbol_candidates (metadata) -> stage-2 symbol addresses -> re.ida.offset for runtime.
4. Decompile only the target methods (headless) rather than the whole multi-MB lib.
5. Record the three-layer map per analyzed method.

skills.name: CTF binary workflow
skills.description: Solve binary challenges with the Ghidra-style flow.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Triage: re.rabin2 -I (arch, stripped?) then re.ghidra.analyze deep=true.
2. Find the win/check function: stage-2 symbols or string pivots (izz~? then axt).
3. Disassemble precisely: re.r2.analyze with pdf @ <symbol>.
4. For decompilation-grade understanding, run headless Ghidra on the challenge (small binaries analyze fast).
5. Extract the logic, compute the solution (python.run_file), verify against the challenge.

skills.name: Version diffing with the pipeline
skills.description: Compare two builds of a native lib.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Run re.ghidra.analyze on both; capture stage-2 symbol lists to workspace files.
2. Diff symbol sets with python.run_file (added/removed/renamed).
3. Compare stage-3 function counts and sizes for changed areas.
4. For changed functions, targeted disassembly (pdf) or headless decompile of both versions.
5. Summarize deltas with engine labels and evidence paths.

skills.name: Evidence chaining (Ghidra flows)
skills.description: Keep headless-pipeline claims reproducible.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Record the exact tool invocations: re.ghidra.analyze(file_path, deep=true) or process.exec analyzeHeadless ... -postScript ...
2. Save stage outputs and headless logs to workspace files; reference paths in the report.
3. Label engine per claim: rabin2 metadata, r2 analysis, Ghidra decompiler, IDA.
4. Re-run the chain before publishing; r2 aaa is deterministic but versions matter.
5. Speculation is labeled speculation — addresses without verification stay hypotheses.

skills.name: Ghidra-style report standards
skills.description: Write professional reports from this pipeline.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Header: target, size, hash, arch, tool/pack versions (ghidra pack 12.1.2 when used), date.
2. Methodology section: which of the 3 stages ran, analysis level (aa vs aaa), and any headless decompilation.
3. Findings: each with symbol, address, stage evidence, and interpretation.
4. Hardening table from stage 1; strings table of interest from stage 3.
5. Appendix: full function inventory reference (workspace file).

skills.name: Large binary strategy
skills.description: Analyze multi-MB libraries sanely.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Never run deep=true as the first step on huge binaries; start with rabin2 metadata only.
2. Use targeted re.r2.analyze command sets (iS; is~Java_; afl~<prefix>) instead of full aaa.
3. If aaa is required, raise max_output and expect a long timeout; run it once and persist the report.
4. Headless Ghidra on large libs: restrict to -processor + address-range scripted exports.
5. Time-box passes; log skipped areas explicitly for later sessions.

skills.name: Honest limits of the approximation
skills.description: Know what the Ghidra-style tool cannot do.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. No real Ghidra decompiler in re.ghidra.analyze itself — it is r2-based approximation output.
2. No data-type/struct recovery engine; struct_recovery (IDA pack) is static heuristics only.
3. No signature analysis (FID), no version tracking, no program diffing — those are desktop-Ghidra features.
4. r2 function detection can split or merge functions differently than Ghidra's analysis; counts are indicative, not canonical.
5. State these limits whenever reports might imply desktop-Ghidra-grade output.

skills.name: Ghidra workflows on your own builds
skills.description: Practice end to end on software you built.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Build a native sample with the NDK pack (clang.exec), keeping symbols unstripped.
2. Run the full pipeline: re.rabin2, re.ghidra.analyze deep=true, then headless Ghidra decompile of a chosen function.
3. Verify the decompiled logic against your original C/C++ source (file.read).
4. Practice the evidence chain: save all outputs, label engines, re-run to confirm reproducibility.
5. This is the recommended sandbox for learning before analyzing unknown binaries.

skills.name: Pipeline troubleshooting
skills.description: Diagnose failures in the Ghidra-style flow.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. r2/rabin2 not found: check the radare2 pack in runtime.info; re-provision if missing.
2. Empty function list after aaa: binary may be packed/stripped; check stage-1 hardening and entropy hints.
3. analyzeHeadless fails: JDK pack missing or GHIDRA_HOME unset; verify both before retrying.
4. Truncated reports: raise max_output or split stage-equivalent runs.
5. Timeouts on aaa: switch to deep=false, or targeted r2 commands; record the partial result.
